newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - July 2.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Air Afrique is ordered to pay 44 million CFA francs ($75,000) in compensation to a Malian fruit exporter that suffered a loss when its produce was not transported on time. The airline has a monopoly on air freight in the countries that own it, including Mali.

- Basic foodstuffs such as bananas and imported rice are becoming too expensive for the average Ivorian. Medicines have soared in price since the 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc, pushing people towards traditional African remedies.

- Mayor of Jacqueville to the west of Abidjan ordered oil prospecting company United Meridian Corp to stop work for a few days at start of June because villagers said locals had not been recruited, amongst other grievances. Work has resumed, while negotiations continue.

- Seven Ivorians from different walks of life say they can see that the economy is picking up, but their own standard of living has not improved, since prices are going up but wages have been more or less frozen.
